html:
In 1793 Captain William Bligh landed breadfruit plants from Tahiti at the botanic garden in Kingstown, St Vincent. His first voyage for them, on the Bounty, had ended in the famous mutiny in 1789.

Planters had asked for the tree as cheap food for the enslaved people on their sugar estates. The St Vincent botanic garden, founded in 1765, is among the oldest in the Americas, and a tree said to come from Bligh's plants still stands there.

At first many enslaved people refused the new food. In time breadfruit became a staple across Jamaica and the islands, roasted, boiled or fried, part of the plant exchange that also took cassava and maize the other way.
